integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, modern vlog style, a handheld medium close-up frames a beautiful 20-year-old Romanian model with voluminous black curly hair and a red dress in a bright morning kitchen. She holds the camera out in one hand at arm's length while holding a black ceramic mug with clear orange text reading "PIXA" in her other hand. She smiles toward the lens, her lips part, and the young woman with a clear, melodic voice and a subtle Eastern European accent (S1) says: <d>[English] I really enjoy my morning coffee.</d> Her jaw and lips move clearly through every word. She then closes her lips into a soft smile, brings the mug toward her chest, and the handheld camera sways slightly with small amplitude at slow speed as steam rises faintly from the cup.

overall_soundscape: Quiet morning kitchen room tone with a distant soft refrigerator hum and faint movement of fabric.

non_diegetic_music: A gentle, upbeat acoustic guitar melody at a relaxed tempo with light percussion, playing softly underneath.

nodes.title: Sampler settings (tested)
widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SAMPLER SETTINGS FOR THE SPEED LORA

Tested on this exact workflow: 54 renders. Six sampler and scheduler pairings, each rendered with 3 different prompts (action close-up, slow snowy portrait, wide aerial city) and 3 different seeds, so a winner had to win repeatedly and not just get lucky once.

The score is out of 10. It rewards a steady picture that does not shimmer, a clean picture without grain, and a small file (a big file at the same size and length means the model spent the bits on noise).

PICK ONE FROM THE DROPDOWN

CombinationScoreWorst runWhat it is good for
euler + simple9.58.0The default here. Won more individual renders outright than anything else.
euler + sgm_uniform9.58.5Tied on average and the most reliable: its worst render is the best worst render. Try it if a clip comes out shimmery.
euler + beta8.56.5Good. Slightly softer look.
dpmpp_sde_gpu + sgm_uniform8.06.5Good, a bit livelier, slower to render.
res_multistep + simple7.54.0Fine on people. Weakest on wide landscapes, where it goes hazy and grainy.


DO NOT USE ddim_uniform

It scored 1.5 out of 10 and it fails in a different way in every kind of shot:

  • Action shot: ignores a request for a close-up and sits back wide, so printed text on clothing comes out small and garbled.
  • Portrait: produced a split frame with the same man twice, plus junk lettering over the picture.
  • Aerial: flew far too low, oversaturated, with a pale artifact stuck in the middle of the shot.

It also makes files about twice the size at the same resolution and length, which is grain, not detail.


WHY THE POPULAR BENCHMARK DISAGREES

The widely shared sampler benchmark puts ddim_uniform pairings in its top three. It is not lying, it is measuring something else: its rating categories are picture quality, motion smoothness, sound and music, and none of them ask whether you got the shot you asked for. A beautiful, smooth video of the wrong thing scores well there. That same post's large sample scheduler ranking agrees with this table and recommends sgm_uniform, simple or beta.



STEPS: USE 8, NOT 4

The LoRA is called a 4 step LoRA and 4 steps is enough for the picture. It is not enough for the sound. Found by blind listening: four clips, same seed, only the step count different, names shuffled and the volume matched so loudness could not give it away. Ranked best to worst, twice, with different seeds:

12 > 8 > 6 > 4 both times. The odds of that happening twice by chance are about 1 in 576.

StepsSoundPictureTime
4Worst, both rounds3.3028sWhat the LoRA is named after
6Third3.2934s
8Second3.3038sUse this. Same picture as 4, better sound, 10 seconds more.
12Best4.2952sSounds best but the picture drifts from your input, on every seed tested

The picture column is how closely the first frame still matches the starting image, lower is better. Notice it is flat from 4 to 8 and then gets worse at 12: the LoRA was distilled for a small number of steps, and 12 pushes it outside what it was trained for.

Measuring tools could NOT find this. Harshness, noisiness and echo were all measured across 54 clips and found nothing, and on echo they pointed the wrong way. Only listening found it.

THE OTHER SETTING THAT MATTERS

The Shift 6 node above the sampler. This LoRA was trained for shift 6, while the model defaults to 12. Leave it at 6.
